document.abstract: This paper provides a snap-shot of the current status of S.M.P.T.E. efforts in the area of digital video component interface standards-for use in studio applications. Electrical and mechanical interface requirements and considerations are given. The technical bases and performance level requirements of CCIR 601, S.M.P.T.E. RP-125, and the current efforts towards a serial digital standard (T14.18-X1) are provided. The relationship between the three documents is also described.

authors.bio: Mr. Baron has over twenty years of experience in the design and development of digital television systems, both in the areas of video processing and synthetic video generation. He has several patents or patent disclosures pending in both of these areas including the patent on the original Vidifont Graphics System, the first of the television Graphics Titling machines and others in the area of temporal filtering. Mr. Baron has been a member of the SMPTE Working Group on Digital Video Standards since 1977, serving as its Chairman since February 1984. He was the Chairman of the subcommittee which drafted the Composite Video document and the Component Digital Video Interface document now being published as RP-125.
